newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lufthansa says airlines panicked over cargo rates.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa says airlines panicked over cargo rates.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo said its partner Cathay Pacific Airways Cargo and other carriers panicked over their ex-Hong Kong to Europe cargo rate pricing policy.

Lufthansa Cargo's general manager for Hong Kong, Macau and South China, Frank Berweger told Reuters in an interview that he seriously questioned why Cathay Cargo and other carriers immediately dropped their ex-Hong Kong cargo rates to Europe as soon as demand fell at the start of May and the traditional slack season.
However Cathay Cargo manager, James Barrington, said the airline had not led the way to lower rates but had followed other airlines.
Hong Kong-based forwarders said the rate dropped by around HK$1.50 to HK$22-23 a kg in the past 10 days.

"I am very disappointed in what has happened and seriously question the pricing strategy, not just of Cathay, but other airlines too. They have been extremely quick to adjust their rates downwards," Lufthansa's Berweger said.

"At the first signs of demand falling they panicked and dropped their rates to amazing levels. I do not understand it because the industry cannot afford to drop rates to the same level as we had last year when yields dropped to such an extent that where some carriers had to question whether they should continue flying or not," Berweger added.
Lufthansa Cargo and Cathay Pacific Cargo operate 11 Boeing 747 freighters a week between Hong Kong and Frankfurt but the operational joint venture does not include pricing policy.
Industry sources said cargo airlines regard Hong Kong's de facto flag carrier as industry leader in the territory and generally follow suit with a rate rises.
Recent statements by Cathay Pacific managers said they would try to improve yields wherever possible and not drop rates unless absolutely necessary.

Cathay's Barrington said : "Everybody always points the finger at somebody. We have taken a strong position and assumed industry leadership not to be the first the airline to drop rates. But at the same time we cannot sit there blindly while other airlines do drop the rates."
"The only reason why Cathay Pacific has dropped its rates is because other airlines, have come down first," Barrington added.

"We want to keep the rates up but it is the off season and there is a bit of spare capacity around and you just can't sit there and let everyone else eat your lunch. We would like to see all the carriers maintaining today's rates but if the big players such as ourselves, Lufthansa and Air France don't, then everyone has to come down," Barrington added.
